title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Amendment Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let the Australian Maritime Safety Authority, acting as national marine safety regulator, reimburse states and the Northern Territory for infringement notice receipts.
It would enable regulations directing penalty payments to the regulator, replacing the Commonwealth as recipient under two provisions of the domestic commercial vessel safety law.
The changes would concern payments offered as alternatives to criminal prosecution or civil penalty proceedings, covering alleged breaches of the national law and its regulations.
changes: Regulations under section 138 could allow an alleged offender to pay the regulator instead of facing prosecution.
Regulations under section 162 could allow payment to the regulator instead of civil penalty proceedings for an alleged regulatory breach.
The payment amendments would begin on royal assent or immediately after section 3 of the national law legislation commences, whichever occurs later.
summary.affected: The Australian Maritime Safety Authority, states, the Northern Territory and people facing infringement notices under domestic commercial vessel safety law are affected.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Introduced a bill amending the Marine Safety National Law to give the Australian Maritime Safety Authority power to reimburse states and the Northern Territory for infringement notice revenue collected under the new single national maritime regulator, which replaces eight existing regulators and commences in March.
